response: Rust does not use a garbage collector. It uses ownership and borrowing, so most memory is freed deterministically at compile-time-managed scope exits, without GC pauses or tracing overhead. Performance still depends on the workload, but that design is a major reason Rust can match C/C++-class performance.

No. A second disk in the same machine can protect against one disk failing, but not theft, fire, power damage, ransomware, accidental deletion, or a machine-wide fault. Keep at least one tested, versioned backup on separate hardware and ideally one off-site or in a separate account.

Regular expressions cannot generally parse arbitrarily nested parentheses because nesting requires unbounded state. Some regex engines add recursion or balancing extensions, but then you are using engine-specific parsing features, not regular-language regex alone. Use a stack-based parser when nesting is part of the input grammar.

Story points are not inherently more accurate than hours; both can be poor estimates when treated as predictions. Keep the historical hours for capacity and delivery analysis, then estimate new work in relative points and calibrate them against completed work over several iterations. Do not convert old hours into points with a fixed ratio.

Lightning can strike the same place repeatedly; tall structures are frequent targets. A lightning-protection system needs more than one rod: correctly placed air terminals, bonded conductors, grounding, surge protection, and design to the applicable local standard. Have a qualified lightning-protection professional assess the building.

No. Publishing secrets can expose systems and data immediately, and hard-coded internal IPs can disclose network details. Remove and rotate every exposed secret before release, scrub repository history, replace environment-specific values with documented configuration, and complete a security and license review first.

Compound interest is exponential because each year's percentage is applied to the current balance, including prior interest. At rate r, a principal P becomes P(1+r)^n after n years. It would be linear only with simple interest, where the percentage is always applied only to the original principal.

100% code coverage does not guarantee the absence of bugs; it only shows that tests executed the covered lines or branches. Use the remaining coverage work to target meaningful scenarios—edge cases, error handling, integration boundaries, and assertions about behavior—rather than treating the percentage as a quality guarantee.
